---
applyTo: 'src/**/*.test.ts,src/test/**'
---

# Tests

- **Layout.** Tests sit next to their module (`ScriptOps.test.ts`). Snapshots live in `src/test/snapshots`, mirroring the source path (resolved by `snapshotResolve.js`); recordings in `src/test/mock-recordings`; staging helpers for recorded tests in `src/test/setup`.
- **Two kinds.** A recorded test calls `autoSetupPolly()` and replays HTTP from recordings. A `*.unit.test.ts` file never uses recordings (none of the 48 does): it injects fakes and needs no tenant.
- **Run** `npm run test:only -- <path pattern>` for a subset and `npm test` for everything. A bare `npx jest` fails without the `--experimental-vm-modules` flag. Tests run on the sources, so they need no build, except two tests in `src/api/BaseApi.connectionReuse.test.ts` that start a child process against `dist/` (run `npm run build` once before the first full `npm test`). The clone directory must be named `frodo-lib`: `src/utils/AutoSetupPolly.ts` finds the recordings through that path segment.
- **A request without a recording fails the test** (`test/jest-polly-replay-integrity.setup.js`). Recording needs a real tenant (`npm run test:record <Name>`, see the header of any recorded test and [RECORD_REPLAY.md](../../RECORD_REPLAY.md)), so a maintainer does it. If your change needs new HTTP traffic, write the test, say in the pull request that it needs a recording, and do not hand-write or edit anything under `src/test/mock-recordings`. The one exception is trimming the repeated polls of a wait recording (decisions/0014).
- **A failing snapshot is either an expected output change or a regression.** Decide which before touching it. Update a snapshot (`npm run test:update`) only for an expected change, and say so in the pull request. Never update snapshots just to turn CI green.
- **Production code does not read the record and replay switches** (`FRODO_MOCK*`, `FRODO_POLLY_MODE`, `FRODO_RECORD_PHASE`). Only `src/api/BaseApi.ts`, `src/utils/AutoSetupPolly.ts`, `src/utils/SetupPollyForFrodoLib.ts` and the helpers in `src/test/setup` do. Do not add another.
- **Tests do not touch the real home directory.** `test/jest-no-real-home.setup.js` makes `os.homedir()`, `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` a fresh temporary directory for each test file and removes it afterwards, so that a default path such as `~/.frodo` (connection profiles, master key, token cache, template catalog cache) lands there. Changing `process.env.HOME` in a test does not reach `os.homedir()`; a test that needs files under the home writes them under `os.homedir()`, and a test of a default path asserts on the path it gets. `src/utils/NoRealHome.guard.unit.test.ts` proves the guard.
- **Tests do not use the proxy of the machine.** `test/jest-no-ambient-proxy.setup.js` removes `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and their lower case forms before each test file and sets `NO_PROXY` to the loopback interface. A test of the proxy support sets the variables it needs and restores them. Proxy support is guarded by the files named in the `npm run test:proxy` script ([decisions/0017](../../decisions/0017-proxy-support-is-guarded-by-a-short-named-set-of-tests.md)); a change to the agent code in `src/api/BaseApi.ts` keeps `npm run test:proxy` passing.
- **Never commit credentials, keys or tokens**, in a test, a fixture or a recording.
